# Group names follow the same rules as user names: an access list holds both
# kinds of name and matches them against each other, so anything illegal as a
# user name is illegal as a group name too.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Telling a user into a group git would never accept as a name.
! exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group 'dev ops'
stderr 'group name'
! exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group 'dev/ops'
stderr 'group name'

# The refused tell left nothing behind - the stage rolled its fork back.
exec sesam user list
! stdout 'bob'
! exists .sesam/signkeys/bob.age

# The same for an access list on a secret.
cp secret db.env
! exec sesam add db.env --group 'dev ops'
stderr 'group name'
exec sesam ls
! stdout 'db\.env'

# A name that follows the rules still works, for both.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev-ops
exec sesam add db.env --group dev-ops
exec sesam ls
stdout 'db\.env'

-- secret --
top secret
